clue.text: Another mug Mum shattered I put in 13

definitions.note: 13 refers to the answer at 13 across, MISCELLANY, of which this is a synonym

indicators.note: put in says the single letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
something shattered is broken into pieces, so these three words are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone breaks yet another of Mum's mugs and confesses to having wedged it into a box of odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' turns ANOTHER MUG MUM into OMNUMGATHERUM; 'put in' slips I in after OMN. The definition is a cross-reference to 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnium-gatherum is a jumble or mixed collection of things, the same idea as a miscellany.

clue.text: Tending to quaver below sheep track, perhaps, when climbing

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece below another comes after it
in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sheep run is an area or track where sheep are kept; perhaps flags the example
to quaver is to sing with a trill or tremble in the voice

explanation.surface: A shepherd, warbling away, follows the path up the hillside while tending the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaver' looks like the musical note but is the verb, to sing tremulously; 'when climbing' reverses only the sheep track, and 'below' places the song after it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing a patient is tending or looking after them.

clue.text: Bone of contention among alumni? I'm staying out of it!

indicators.note: contention means strife or disorder, so the letters are thrown into disarray
says the letters of I'm are kept out, leaving the rest of alumni to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Old students squabble over a bone of contention, and the speaker refuses to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and M out of ALUMNI to leave ALUN, and 'of contention' scrambles those letters. 'Bone of contention' looks like a single idiom, but only 'Bone' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Inclination to stop working in conveyance

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: in law a grant is a conveyance, the transfer of property by deed
a machine that stops working is said to die

explanation.surface: Someone feels the urge to quit their job while travelling in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveyance' suggests a vehicle; here it is the legal sense, a GRANT of property.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, the degree to which a road or line is inclined.

clue.text: Maybe three adjacent diamonds rank above hearts in Jack's judgement?

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece above another comes before it

parts.note: a tier is a rank or level in a hierarchy

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, taken here from each of the two words

explanation.surface: A card player wonders whether a run of diamonds outranks hearts, in Jack's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts in' takes the middle letters C (from JACK'S) and E (from JUDGEMENT). 'diamonds' and 'hearts' both look like card suits, but only the first belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as piquet, a tierce is a sequence of three cards of one suit; maybe signals an example.

clue.text: During troublesome teens, Miss Malone reportedly obtains calmatives

definitions.note: plural noun, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: during says the name goes inside, occurring in the middle of the other piece
troublesome teens are unruly, so the letters of teens are jumbled
reportedly says the name is taken by how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Molly Malone is the fishmonger of the Dublin song Cockles and Mussels

explanation.surface: During their difficult teenage years, a girl called Miss Malone is said to get hold of sedatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublesome' scrambles the teens to wrap round the name; Molly Malone is the heroine of the Irish song Cockles and Mussels, and 'reportedly' lets her name be spelt the way it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Emollients are soothing agents, literally for the skin and figuratively for tempers, so they work as calming things.

clue.text: Steal the show in hill climb on the Tour?

definitions.meaning: to draw attention away from them
read as ..., a stage of the Tour de France that goes uphill

explanation.surface: A cyclist wins the mountain stage of the Tour de France and grabs the headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage a fellow actor is to move upstage so they must turn away from the audience, stealing attention; the split reading is a climbing stage.

clue.text: Might cast members be childhood chums?

definitions.text: Might cast members be childhood chums?

parts.words: Might cast members be childhood chums?
parts.note: actors cast in the same play could whimsically be called fellows of the play, which splits the answer word for childhood companions

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the actors in a production grew up together.
explanation.definitionFit: Playfellows are companions children play with, so childhood chums; the clue jokes on fellows in a play.

clue.text: Chase puss into the empty dock

indicators.note: into says the pieces go inside the other piece
an empty word has lost its inside, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: to chase is to run after
puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: An instruction to chase the cat into a deserted harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the outer letters of 'the'. 'dock' looks like a harbour but is the verb, to cut short, as with a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail is to cut it short, which is to truncate it.

clue.text: Winger from Oxford United scores early on — Rochdale successful finally

indicators.note: early on points to the start of each of the three words
finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A football report: a wide player for Oxford United scores early on, but Rochdale win in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a football wide player; it is a bird. Oxford United and Rochdale are English football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird and related birds, and a bird is a winged creature.

clue.text: I'm a fall guy, thrown around right into 13

definitions.note: 13 refers to the answer at 13 across, MISCELLANY, of which this is a synonym

indicators.note: into says the letter is put inside the rearranged letters
being thrown around jumbles these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A stuntman confesses he is the fall guy who keeps getting thrown about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown around' turns I'M A FALL GUY into GALLIMAUFY, and 'into' puts R before the final Y. The definition is a cross-reference to 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallimaufry is a jumble or medley of things, so a mixed assortment like a miscellany.

clue.text: Passage of time following Ms Lupino's retirement

indicators.note: the letter for time follows, coming after the name
retirement means withdrawal or going back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ida Lupino was a British-born Hollywood actress and director

explanation.surface: A spell of time after an actress has retired from the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage of time' looks like one phrase, but only 'Passage' is the definition; 'retirement' signals the actress's first name read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage leading into a mine.

clue.text: Miss Fitzgerald, we hear, is going to the Big Apple, appearing in variety

indicators.note: we hear says the words are taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was the great American jazz singer
the Big Apple is a nickname for New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: Ella Fitzgerald heads for New York to appear in a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS ELLA said aloud gives MISCELLA. 'variety' looks like a variety show, but it means an assortment.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixture of assorted items, which is a variety.

clue.text: Little choir in stew with church for 13

definitions.note: 13 refers to the answer at 13 across, MISCELLANY, of which this is a synonym

indicators.note: with joins the final abbreviation onto the end
in says the abbreviation goes inside the stew

parts.note: a hotpot is a meat and potato stew, a Lancashire dish
little signals the abbreviation CH for choir

explanation.surface: A small church choir finds itself in a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in stew' looks like 'in trouble'. A hotpot is a British stew of meat under sliced potatoes; 'in' and 'with' place the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch is a confused mixture of things, so it is a jumbled collection like a miscellany.

clue.text: Birds in boaters?

definitions.meaning: leghorn is a fine plaited straw used for hats, and boaters are straw hats

explanation.surface: A whimsical image of birds riding in boats or wearing straw hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Leghorns are a chicken breed and also straw hats, both named after the Italian port of Livorno.

clue.text: Drastic cut by base

indicators.note: by places the letter alongside, after the previous piece

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A harsh reduction made at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' suggests a military site; it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and drastic both describe measures that are extreme or harsh.

clue.text: Close friend of Edward, say, enthralled by voice

indicators.note: enthralled by says these letters are held captive inside the voice

parts.note: an alto is a singing voice
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A close friend of a man named Edward is captivated by someone's singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edward' gives the royal cipher for King Edward rather than a nickname, and 'enthralled by' holds it with the example abbreviation inside the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is literally a second self, used for a trusted, intimate friend.

clue.text: Doctor, doctor — I'd come!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient calls for a doctor, who answers that they will come.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'doctor' looks like a cry for help; the first is the definition, the second tells you to rearrange I'D COME.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is an informal word for a doctor or medical student.

clue.text: Top game from Verdi, a Bolognese by extraction

indicators.note: extraction says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Verdi described as a native of Bologna, by birth or ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by extraction' reads as family origin; here it signals taking the answer out of the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which a two-headed spinning top is tossed on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: Inactive husband with terrible flu's next to window

indicators.note: next to says the following pieces sit beside the first

parts.note: a slot is a window of time, as in a time slot

indicators.note: a terrible condition is in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word flu, with 's read as is, a link joining it to the rest

explanation.surface: A husband laid up with a bad dose of flu sits idly by the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns FLU into FUL. 'window' looks like a pane of glass, but it is a time slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Slothful means lazy and sluggish, so idle or inactive.

clue.text: Republican parts very much earlier in 13

definitions.note: 13 refers to the answer at 13 across, MISCELLANY, of which this is a synonym

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the phrase opens to take the letter

parts.note: far ago, a long time before, means very much earlier

explanation.surface: A Republican politician parts company with others much earlier on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' splits FAR AGO to put R between FAR and AGO. The definition is a cross-reference to 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or medley, a muddled assortment like a miscellany.

clue.text: Six-footer's remarkable stamina — there's only one answer to that!

definitions.note: reads as six-footer is, the definition plus a link

indicators.note: read as re-markable, able to be marked again, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer; only one means one of the two As in stamina is dropped

explanation.surface: A tall person shows great endurance, and someone insists there is no more to be said.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one A from STAMINA, as 'only one answer' asks, and rearrange the rest. 'Six-footer' looks like a tall person but means an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantis, such as the praying mantis, is an insect, and insects have six legs.

clue.text: Receiving no satisfaction from a French program, took it gently

parts.note: un is French for a
an app is a computer program
eased means went slowly or gently

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated with a French app that runs too slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'program' is spelt the computing way; it is an APP.
explanation.definitionFit: Unappeased means not satisfied or placated.

clue.text: Stem or stalk pruned

indicators.note: something pruned has been cut back, here losing its final letter

parts.note: to stalk is to prowl after prey

explanation.surface: A gardener trims back a plant's stem or stalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stem' and 'stalk' look like plant parts. 'Stem' is the bow of a ship, and 'stalk' is the verb, PROWL, losing its L.
explanation.definitionFit: The stem of a ship is its bow, the foremost part, also called the prow.

clue.text: Hardy sergeant's weight

definitions.meaning: Sergeant Frank ... is the dashing soldier in Thomas Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd
... weight is the system used for precious metals

explanation.surface: How heavy a tough army sergeant is.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy names both a character in Hardy's novel and the measurement system for gold and silver.

clue.text: Component of not-so-ordinary reversible bed

indicators.note: reversible says the hidden letters are read backwards
a component is a part, so the answer is a part of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: An unusual bed that can be flipped over, sold as a flat-pack part.
explanation.walkthrough: TSOOR sits inside NOT-SO-ORDINARY, and 'reversible' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds rest or sleep, so it is a bird's bed.

clue.text: One decides to unite with bill embracing resistance

parts.note: to tie is to join or unite

indicators.note: embracing says the outer word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A politician resolves to back a bill despite opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a parliamentary bill; it is a bird's BEAK, holding R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreak is the extra game or question that settles a drawn contest.

clue.text: Those oysters go off, they say

indicators.note: food that has gone off has spoiled, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A warning that the oysters spoil quickly, or so people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: So the story goes is an idiom meaning reportedly, according to what people say.
